- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to undercorrect — force upward adjustment in forecast mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and continues upward trend — cap growth rate at 2–3% per day post-spike.
- In high-bearish event context (bearish > 30, supply net < -15), model underestimates downside — add 1–2% downward bias to 30d forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model fails to recognize mean reversion — apply slight upward bias to offset overcorrection.
- When official events are frequent and bearish, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true price drop to account for event momentum.
- In low-bullish/high-bearish context, model often ignores sentiment — if sentiment > 0.67, model must adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bearish sentiment weight.
